properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: DIVERSIFIED PROD LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 4/06/2023
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 991056
Permit API: 005-29235
Unconventional: No
County: Armstrong
Municipality: Gilpin Twp
Inspection Type: Compliance Evaluation
Inspection Date: 4/06/2023
Comments: On Thursday, 4/6/2023, I conducted a compliance evaluation inspection of the Diversified Production, LLC McIntyre 1 well, permit number 005-29235. The well is located in the woods off of Coal Bank Road in Gilpin township, Armstrong county. The previous inspection, inspection id # 3472682, conducted on 12/14/2022, resulted in violations being cited due to a broken pipe from the separator to the brine tank. This caused brine to be sprayed onto the brine tank and ground. Violations to 25 PA Code 78.54, 25 PA Code 78.57(a), SWMA 301, SWMA 302(A), SWMA 610(1), and CSL 402(b) were cited as a result of these conditions. The operator has since replaced the pipe to the brine tank, removed the contaminated soil, and restored the area affected by the sprayed brine. The violations to 25 PA Code 78.54, 25 PA Code 78.57(a), SWMA 610(1), and CSL 402(b) have been closed as the operator has corrected these deficiencies. The operator has collected the contaminated soils in 5 gallon buckets that remain onsite. The violations to SWMA 301 and SWMA 302(A) remain outstanding as a result of the operator's failure to remove and properly dispose of the contaminated soil, and provide proof of proper disposal to the Department, as was requested in the previous inspection report. The operator has placed stone/gravel onto an area of the access road, stabilizing an area of standing/ponded water noted in the previous inspection, correcting this deficiency. There are no new violations being cited for this inspection. The violations to SWMA 301 and SWMA 302(A) remain outstanding.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 2020-01-27 to Howard Drilling Inc in Conemaugh Twp, Indiana county. 78.64(a) - CONTAINMENT AROUND OIL TANKS - For a tank capacity of at least 660 gallons or tanks with a combined capacity of at least 1,320 gallons, the owner or operator failed to construct and maintain a dike or other method of secondary containment which satisfies requirements under 40 CFR 112.

Report Details

Violation Code: 78.64(a) - CONTAINMENT AROUND OIL TANKS - For a tank capacity of at least 660 gallons or tanks with a combined capacity of at least 1,320 gallons, the owner or operator failed to construct and maintain a dike or other method of secondary containment which satisfies requirements under 40 CFR 112.
Violation ID: 875278
Permit API: 063-32818
Unconventional: No
County: Indiana
Municipality: Conemaugh Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2020-01-27
Comments: On 1/27/19 at 0945 hrs., I conducted an inspection in response to a crude oil release that was reported to the Department on 1/25/20, and initially was discovered on 1/24/20. The release occurred near Howard Drilling, Inc.'s TLC 1 well (API 063-32818) in Conemaugh Twp., Indiana Co. According to initial reports, and verified by Mr. Dale "Wally" Howard via telephone on 1/27/20, approximately 80 barrels of crude oil was transferred from stock tanks at two nearby wells (063-22666 and 063-31878) during plugging operations, to two 100 barrel holding tanks located adjacent to Hogue Drive. According to Mr. Howard, the holding tanks belong to Tunnelton Liquids Company (property owner). ARG Refining was scheduled to pick the oil up on 1/24/20. The driver notified Howard Drilling on 1/24/20 that the tanks were empty. The driver then walked over to the release area and confirmed that crude oil had been released from the tanks, but was uncertain of he extent of the release. Mr. Howard had crews onsite on 1/24/20 and notified the Department of the release on 1/25/20. According to Mr. Howard, the driver reported that the valve to the tanks was open and a hose was connected to the tank valve and led to a drain in the adjacent cement pad. The crude oil flowed through the drain, under Hogue Drive and around a concrete secondary containment structure. The oil then flowed South through an old mine drainage treatment pond, and into a canal, which drains to the Conemaugh. McCutcheon Enterprises was contracted by Howard Drilling on 1/25/20 to begin the cleanup process. During my inspection, McCutcheon was in the process of excavating surface soils. In addition to the excavation, McCutcheon was also going to replace the underflow dam with one made of sand-filled super sacs. There was concern that the original dam was constructed with contaminated soil and this material was to be removed. McCutcheon was also conducting boom maintenance along the spill path. During my inspection, it was evident that some residual crude material remained in the drainage canal south of the release site; however, had still not made it to the down-gradient culvert leading to the Conemaugh River. The release of crude oil onto the ground and into waters of the Commonwealth constitutes violations of CSL 301, CSL 307(a), 78.57(a), SWMA 301, SWMA 302(A), and SWMA 610(1). Failure to immediately notify the Department of the release constitutes violations of 91.33(A) and 78.66(a). These violations have been closed as "unresolvable". Failure to have adequate secondary containment around the tanks constitutes a violation of 78.64(a). The existing containment structure was backfilled and did not have sufficient capacity to prevent the release from impacting waters of the Commonwealth. This constitutes a violation of 78.64(b). You are hereby requested to follow Department Policy 800-5000-001, Addressing Spills and Releases at Oil & Gas Well Sites or Access Roads. This Policy sets forth he procedures that should be followed to resolve the violations associated with the release noted in this Notice of Violation by using either the Act 2 or Alternative Remediation Process. A copy of the Policy is attached for your review.

properties.title: PA Permit Violation Issued to PA GEN ENERGY CO LLC in Keating Twp, Potter County
properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 5/11/2022 to PA GEN ENERGY CO LLC in Keating Twp, Potter county. 78a64a(f) - SECONDARY CONTAINMENT – Operator failed to remove regulated substances that escaped from primary containment or otherwise spilled onto secondary containment as soon as possible and inspect the secondary containment after removal.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: PA GEN ENERGY CO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 5/11/2022
Violation Code: 78a64a(f) - SECONDARY CONTAINMENT – Operator failed to remove regulated substances that escaped from primary containment or otherwise spilled onto secondary containment as soon as possible and inspect the secondary containment after removal.
Violation ID: 955460
Permit API: 105-21845
Unconventional: Yes
County: Potter
Municipality: Keating Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 5/11/2022
Comments: The Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an INCIDENT inspection of the PGE – Hancock Pad A located in Keating Twp, Potter Co. on 5/12/22 @1210 hours in response to a reported release of approximately 10 barrels of brine to the pad surface (CID#364034). The weather was 73 degrees, sunny, winds ENE@3mph. Mr. Chad Earley, PGE HSE Supervisor and Mr. Matt Covine, PGE Completions Consultant were present onsite for the inspection. Mr. Earley stated a cement truck was parked in secondary containment yesterday during the previous days plugging activities. A brine solution was spilled into the secondary containment from the truck. At the end of yesteday’s plugging activities, the secondary containment was "almost full" of the brine solution. The brine solution was left in the secondary containment overnight. Mr. Earley stated when Mr. Covine arrived onsite the next morning, there was less brine solution in the secondary containment and visible staining and fluid on the pad surface. Mr. Earley estimates 10 barrels of fluid was released to the pad surface. I screened the fluid remaining in the secondary containment with an Oakton Multiparameter meter. The field conductivity was measured at 18.8mS/cm. Damp areas around the secondary containment were screened with a Groline soil conductivity meter and found to be >4.0mS/cm. Two vac trucks arrived onsite to remove the fluid remaining in the secondary containment as well as the brine solution remaining in the two water tanks adjacent to the spill area. The secondary containment responsible for the release was lifted with a telehandler and the underside examined. The Secondary containment appeared to have a seam that was not properly sealed, this allowed fluid to leak from the bottom of the containment. The visibly impacted area was estimated to cover ~20’ long x 12’ wide. As material was excavated and placed into a lined rolloff waste container, a clay layer was encountered approximately 14" below the pad surface. Mr. Earley screened the clay material with a field conductivity meter and found the material measured <500uS/cm. Mr. Earley stated the clay later appeared to be a barrier for further infiltration of the brine solution. Mr. Earley also stated the brine solution appeared to have laterally migrated under the brine tank containment adjacent to the excavated spill area. Mr. Earley stated their plan was to excavate the 12’ x 20’ impacted area, while field screening, to ensure all impacted areas are identified. PGE would then line the area with plastic and backfill with clean gravel to accommodate completion of the plugging activity. Mr. Earley stated PGE would then have the tanks and their containment removed to further screen the area under the tanks and remove any additional impacted material. I requested Mr. Earley email me pictures of today's completed cleanup activities and provided my contact information. Due to the reported volume of the release being greater than 42 gallons the operator must demonstrate attainment of one or more of the standards established by Act 2 and Chapter 250. This incident is referred to the DEP Cleanups Program for Follow-up. Violations of the following regulations are cited against the Hancock Pad A 2741 Well (API#105-21845) at this time: 25 Pa Code 78a.64(b) 25 Pa Code 78a.64(f) CSL 402(b) SWMA 301 I departed the site at 1440 hours.

Comments: On March 27, 2023, I conducted an inspection of the Shotski 7H well in Somerset Township, Washington County. The inspection was conducted in response to a release reported to the Department on 3/25/2023. The report indicted that approximately 5-10 gallons of production fluid was released from a washed out pipe within GPU 7.The Act 9 site ID, PPC plan and ER plan were on site.At the time of inspection the Operator was decommissioning the GPUs. According to the on site representative the GPUs will be removed from the location and replaced.I observed staining and excavation around the 7H GPU. I utilized a conductivity probe to collect readings within the impacted area (photos 7,8 and 9).The impacted area appeared to be approximately 20' wide and 40' long and 2 to 12 inched in depth. The 7H GPU did not appear to be contained within secondary containment. The Shotski wells are not included within the 12/17/2020 Secondary Containment COA. I also collected a conductivity reading within the 7H self contained GPU (photo 13).The release appears to be contained to the well pad surface. Violation are being issued for failure to control a regulated fluid and failure to design and construct the well site with secondary containment.

All slam bar holes at the time of inspection were non-detect for combustible gas. As of the completion of this inspection, the operator has not plugged the well nor remedied any of the outstanding violations associated with the well. A previous check valve violation created in error has been closed.

Comments: On Wednesday February 27, 2019 I received notification of a release of produced fluid at the Rogersville/Shumaker Well Site located in Center Township, Greene County. The release was identified and reported to the Department the previous day at approximately 1739 hours. On Wednesday morning I conducted an incident inspection to assess the situation. While on-site, I spoke on the telephone with Mr. Corey Giles from EQT Production Company (EQT) regarding details of the release and subsequent remediation. The release occurred as a result of a dump valve wash-out in the GPU associated with the 9H gas well (059-26433). EQT estimated that approximately 14 gallons of produced water was released due to the wash-out. properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 10/25/2024 to BEAR LAKE PROP LLC in Columbus Township, Warren county. CSL 307(a) - INDUSTRIAL WASTE DISCHARGES - Industrial waste discharged, directly or indirectly, into Waters of the Commonwealth, without a permit, authorization, or contrary to rules and regulations of the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: BEAR LAKE PROP LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 10/25/2024
Violation Code: CSL 307(a) - INDUSTRIAL WASTE DISCHARGES - Industrial waste discharged, directly or indirectly, into Waters of the Commonwealth, without a permit, authorization, or contrary to rules and regulations of the Department.
Violation ID: 8206013
Permit API: 123-39874
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Columbus Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Partial Inspection
Inspection Date: 10/25/2024
Comments: The Bittinger 4 disposal injection well is housed inside a shed and is plumbed directly to the Bear Lake Properties, LLC truck unloading area located approximately 1500 feet east of the Bittinger 4 well. Multiple pieces of liner have been placed on the floor of the shed around the well. At this time, standing fluid was visible on the liner. A conductivity meter was used to find that the fluid's conductivity was greater than 20,000 microsiemens per centimeter (uS/cm). The partially exposed dirt floor at the edge of the liner was found to have soils with conductivity greater than 1,000 uS/cm, with some measurements as high as 2,500 uS/cm being observed. The fluid originating from Bittinger 4 traveled southwest from the shed to the edge of the gravel well pad, as evident from the dead vegetation and exposed soils in this direction. The portion of the gravel pad downslope of the shed was noticeably wet despite recent lack of rain. Approximately three feet southwest of the shed, a conductivity reading of 4,000 uS/cm was observed a few inches below the surface of the gravel. Approximately 70 feet southwest of the shed, soil conductivity of 2,330 uS/cm was observed in soils at the edge of the gravel pad.Background soil conductivity measurements were taken across portions of the site in areas that appeared to be unaffected by the release of fluids from Bittinger 4. Background soil conductivity readings between 200 to 300 uS/cm were observed at apparently unimpacted areas near the Bittinger 4 location.After encountering a depression at the edge of the gravel pad, the flow of the fluid was redirected southward. The southward flow was apparent via swaths of dead vegetation and bare soils that appeared to broaden in size and meander about following the terrain. This anastomosing continued for approximately 250 feet between the edge of the gravel pad to where a utility pole was located downslope of Bittinger 4. Near the utility pole, the flow of fluid again channelized and continued approximately 250 feet further down an ATV trail. At this point, as observed by dead vegetation, the majority of the released fluids crossed over the ATV trail and entered a natural drainage swale.Standing water in the drainage swale was found to have an elevated conductivity of 6,100 uS/cm. Soils in the swale were also observed to have elevated conductivity. The impact to this swale continue for approximately 500 feet before the swale transitions into an unnamed tributary (UNT) of Brokenstraw Creek.Approximately 700 feet from the point at which the swale transitions into the UNT of Brokenstraw Creek, another stream channel converges with the impacted stream. Conductivity readings in the UNT of Brokenstraw Creek remain downstream from the confluence of the channels with levels observed greater than 1,000 uS/cm. In contrast, water conductivity measured approximately ten feet upstream of the confluence in the unaffected channel was 130 uS/cm.The apparent extent of impact to the UNT of Brokenstraw Creek ends at a point with coordinates reading 41.99407 degrees North by 79.54025 degrees West.On 10/25/24 I called and spoke with John McCollums of Bear Lake Properties, LLC to request that the source and extent of the release be identified to prevent further pollution. John agreed to meet with Department officials early next week to review the release.A Notice of Violations (NOV) is included as part of this inspection. Please refer to the NOV for additional information regarding cleanup expectations.

Soils in the swale were also observed to have elevated conductivity. The impact to this swale continue for approximately 500 feet before the swale transitions into an unnamed tributary (UNT) of Brokenstraw Creek.Approximately 700 feet from the point at which the swale transitions into the UNT of Brokenstraw Creek, another stream channel converges with the impacted stream. Conductivity readings in the UNT of Brokenstraw Creek remain downstream from the confluence of the channels with levels observed greater than 1,000 uS/cm. In contrast, water conductivity measured approximately ten feet upstream of the confluence in the unaffected channel was 130 uS/cm.The apparent extent of impact to the UNT of Brokenstraw Creek ends at a point with coordinates reading 41.99407 degrees North by 79.54025 degrees West.On 10/25/24 I called and spoke with John McCollums of Bear Lake Properties, LLC to request that the source and extent of the release be identified to prevent further pollution. John agreed to meet with Department officials early next week to review the release.A Notice of Violations (NOV) is included as part of this inspection. Please refer to the NOV for additional information regarding cleanup expectations.

Comments: This well was drilled in an agricultural area off of Cider Mill Road in November/December 2007.On 10/24/22, an NOV was issued to Stonehaven Energy when it was discovered that the brine tank had been allowed to overflow. On 3/27/23, an administrative order was issued due to a lack of remedial action from Stonehaven Energy. This order was delivered in person by Bureau of Investigations staff on 3/28/2023. No soil sample documentation has been received by the Department as of this date, and heavy deer tracks at the restored site indicate that there may still be some residual contamination. All documentation regarding the Act 2 clean-up of this site should be submitted to the Department as soon as it is available.The well has been tagged with the correct DEP permit number. The original violations regarding the spill at the site have been superseded by the administrative order.Since the most recent inspection of this site on 12/6/2023 (Inspection Record # 3655836), there have been no changes at the site. New violations have been issued during this inspection for failure to comply with an issued court order, failure to plug the well upon abandonment, and for failure to submit annual production information.

properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Xto Energy Inc
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2019-11-04
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 867187
Permit API: 035-21316
Unconventional: Yes
County: Clinton
Municipality: Chapman Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 2019-11-04
Comments: I arrived on site and met Nate Veneziano, Clint Stoltzfus, and George Winebark of XTO. Zachary Lieb and Brynn Yochim of Moody & Associates were also present. Sitewide containment was being removed and the pad screened to identify areas in need of excavation due to the produced water release identified on 5/28/19 by Brad Kline, WQS for the Department. Containment removal began to the north of the wellheads, working clockwise around them. Zach and Brynn began their conductivity screening on the west edge of the pad where high conductance fluid was moving off the pad; distressed vegetation in this area appears to have recovered. Very little water was present on the north side of the wellheads, and soil and water conductance in this area was low (.2-.4 mS/cm) with the exception of an area bare of gravel approximately 10' east by northeast of the wells. This area showed soil conductance of 1.98 mS/cm. To the east of the wellheads, what appeared to be several petroleum stains were present, and one very small (less than 1 quart) puddle showed high conductance (16.50 mS/cm). Other puddles in close proximity showed low conductance (.65-1.2 mS/cm). To the south of the wells between the wells and the produced water Baker tank battery, water was puddled nearly everywhere; conductance reading were low (.185-.235 mS/cm). When I departed, containment had not yet been removed to the west of the wellheads; as this was the potential flow path of the release, this area should be screened thoroughly.

Comments: Site inspection conducted to review residual waste processing activities at the EQT COP 551B pad with EQT Company Man Bill Mitchell. Weather at time of inspection is partly sunny and 46 degrees F. According to Mr. Mitchell, Precision Drilling Rig #110 is currently drilling the 6H well at a depth of 6378'. This is the 7th well of 9 total to be drilled during this setup. Drilling resumed on the 6H well on 10/15 and the well is being drilled using Water Based Mud to kickoff point at 8650' where the rig will be switched over to Synthetic OBM. The anticipated Total Depth of the 6H well is 22897'. All nine wells have been batch drilled to the intermediate depth. The 7H well was recently completed and cemented on 10/13. Clean Harbors Backyard Crew is processing the drill cuttings in the rig backyard. Three shale shakers and three drying shakers are active. Polymer flocculant is being added to the drilling mud during this inspection before it is run through the centrifuge. One centrifuge is removing cuttings from the drilling mud. An excavator is mixing wood pellets into the drill cuttings to solidify the material for landfill disposal. Prior to site transfer to EQT, ARD submitted a Request for Approval for Previously Approved Alternative Waste Management Practices (OG71) Form B for this well pad on 2/2/2021. The Department approved the request on 2/3/2021. The intent of onsite drill cuttings processing is to separate the solid fraction of the cuttings from reusable drilling mud fluid so fluids can be returned to mud tanks for further drilling activity. For further information, refer to the COP Tract 357 Pad A OG-71 Form A application regarding drill cuttings processing (EFACTS authorization #1300435). During this inspection, fluid with a sheen is observed within tertiary containment outside the OBM tanks. The Department recommends that containment structures be vacuumed and fluids be sent for treatment or disposal. The original trench sump collecting runoff along the access road near the mud tanks has a field conductivity reading of 733 uS/cm. There Re no new violations noted during this inspection. Violations remain outstanding on Pad B based on Inspection Report #3231577 by DEP WQS Brad Kline dated 8/9/21.

Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 3/21/2023
Comments: On 3/21/2023, DEP representative John Rogers conducted an incident - response to an accident or event inspection at the Chesapeake Hopson well site. On 3/18/2023 Chesapeake reported that 10 gallons of produced water sprayed out of a damaged pipe on a GPU unit, the water impacting the unprotected pad surface. Creston Environmental identified the extent of the impacted area and excavation was scheduled for 3/20/2023. It was 39 degrees and clear when I arrived on location.When I first arrived at the site, I met Chesapeake's Pat Adams who described activities with the event. Pat showed me a pipe nipple on the 1HC GPU that had been replaced. He showed me the excavated area that is in the northeast corner of the site. The excavated hole had not been backfilled at the time of the inspection. The excavated area is roughly 12' x 40' with various depths up to 2', running along the edge of the perimeter berm. The GPU had been moved from the affected area and had not been returned back to its original position. Pat said that a truck driver first witnessed the spill. Upon discovery, all ten wells were shut in. Pat had just put the 9 unaffected wells back into production before my arrival. The 1HC was still shut in until the GPU is reinstalled. The excavated material remains on site and has been piled on a plastic sheet on the southeast corner of the pad. I field tested some small water puddles in the bottom of the excavated area with results being as high as 4.18 mS conductance. Using a Hanna Gro-line soil probe, I probed the side of the excavated area with one reading being 1.03 mS conductance. I discussed the elevated conductance of the water and soil with Chesapeake's Eric Hottenstein. Eric said he would have someone probe the excavated area to determine if further excavation was necessary. Violation Code: 78.54 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS - Operator failed to control and dispose of fluids, residual waste and drill cuttings, including tophole water, brines, drilling fluids, drilling muds, stimulation fluids, well servicing fluids, oil, and production fluids in a manner that prevents pollution of the waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 948068
Permit API: 083-49666
Unconventional: No
County: McKean
Municipality: Hamilton Twp
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/15/2022
Comments: This inspection was performed following a report of an oil and gas leak in the vicinity of Chappel Fork near the road crossing of RT 321 (CTS #362745). At the time of the report to DEP, I spoke to the complainant and determined the location to begin searching. I contacted Pennhills Resources as they have wells in the immediate vicinity, and we agreed to meet on site to look. After beginning at Rt 321 we headed east until we found some oil collected in a low spot. It appears as though a line has burst with some gas pressure on the line, causing oil and gas to bubble to the surface. The oil then flowed south and into a low swale, where the majority of it collected. Some crude then flowed through into a channel formed by the collection of two spring runs, and toward the main branch of Chappel Fork. Oil was collecting behind ice pockets and in between leaves and dead vegetation for approximately 200 feet. A small amount of sheen was noted in Chappel Fork, but no free product. Approximately 15-20 barrels of oil was emitted from the line in total. Another small area nearer to the creek when following the line was noted to contain some basic sediment and paraffin at the surface and under a hemlock tree; it is uncertain if this is another leak site or simply product following the line. Pennhills immediately moved to contain the spill with booms in the back channel, and then brought a mini excavator to site to dig up the line and slow the leak. The 2" line was uncovered and a band placed on the line, which was broken on the bottom. It was determined that the old access past well 9A could be used to mobilize equipment and some brush was removed to make for better access. A vac truck was brought to site to collect any free product available, which was able to get a large amount on the first load. It was determined the evening of 3/15 that the line belonged to Pennhills, who will be continuing to clean up the oil and soil until clean. The operator built two underflow dams to contain any free product flowing down the channel with melting ice starting to give way. Followup inspection will be performed as necessary.

Unconventional: No
County: Armstrong
Municipality: South Bend Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/15/2022
Comments: This is a Coal bed methane well near an area where a water diminution issue was occurring. At the time of inspection, well was equipped to produce. It was hooked up to a pump jack which starts automatically. The well had 2 3/8" for the water to be transported to the tanks. This valve was closed. There was a T in the line that led below ground. Prior to that, there was a valve leaking significant amounts of water to the ground. I would estimate 1/2 to 1 gallon per minute was leaking. There were three 100 bbl poly tanks tied in. The 4 1/2" is being used as the production string and the valve was pinched open. It led to another check valve and a meter that was telematic. The 4 1/2" annulus (inside the 7") was open to atmosphere. No gas was detected. The 7" annulus could be seen at surface. It was full of water; no bubbles were seen. The well integrity appeared to be in good condition, showing some minor corrosion as rust, but no signs of leaks were noticed. The water is a produced fluid from the well and is required by the regulations to be collected in an approved manner such as tank. Therefore, a violation has occurred and an NOV processed.

Comments: This conventional well is equipped with rods and tubing. The pump jack has been removed from the well, the annulus of the well remains connected to a gathering line. There was no activity onsite during this inspection. The well is not equipped with a well tag, nor is there a site ID sign posted at the location.A tank battery containing four steel tanks and two poly tanks inside of an earthen containment is located approximately 200 feet east of this well. There are indications that production fluids (primarily brine) have repeatedly been released onto the gravel inside of this containment. The soil is stained and specific conductance of the soil is elevated at the western edge where fluid from the tanks appears to have been released, and at the eastern edge of the containment where fluids appear to have been released from a pipeline riser/blow off).Vegetation is absent and deer tracks are very dense on the surface outside of the west/northwest extent of the containment, as it appears the released fluids have migrated through the earthen walls at the natural contour onto which the gravel and earthen wells were constructed. Stained soil and elevated specific conductance continue westward into a roadside ditch of Forest Road 219 until the ditch reaches a cross culvert approximately 300 feet away.Multiple sections of the Warrant 2980 lease roads beyond this well to the vicinity of well #'s 053-29931, 053-29930, 053-29944, 053-29955 and 053-29945 have not been sufficiently maintained. BMPs (ditches and cross culverts) that are installed along these roads are not functioning properly, as a result, accelerated erosion is occurring over various stretches of the road surface. These E and S concerns are considered part of E and S violations that are documented in the 5/11/23 inspection report for 053-29816 (Warrant 2980 #45).It is requested that documentation of production water disposal from this lease be provided to the Department. Please see the attached Notice of Violation regarding requested information pertaining to the cause of the release and intentions to remediate the contaminated material within and outside of the tank battery.

Comments: On March 17, 2025, the Department conducted a routine inspection. Well is tagged, but tag is broken and thus does not display API number. Other piece of the tag is not observed on site at this time. Well posting is not observed on site. Well is located behind a large trailer covered in tarp and sitting on a cement pad. It is not clear what type of trailer this is or what is under the tarp. Three tanks are observed on site.- The first tank (Photos 5-8) is labeled 'Water' and is closed top and appears to be closed off with a cap at a valve at the bottom of the tank. A well tag is affixed to this tank with the API number of a different well (129-25077)- The second tank (Photos 9-13) is open top with fluid inside, nearly filled to the top of the tank and appears to be closed off with a cap at the bottom of the tank. Fluid inside is unidentified, but is brown in color, possibly due to rusting inside.- The third tank (Photos 15-19) is open top on one end, is open at the bottom near the valve and is not holding fluid at this time.Specific conductivity was measured on site. Background readings are approximately around 200 uS. Reading near each of the tanks are also approximately around 200 uS. It does not appear as though a release has occurred on site at this time. No production equipment is observed on site at this time. Disconnected lines and piping is observed on site. Black and orange lines are observed to be disconnected from the well and appear to possibly be old gathering lines. Other piping is observed, which appears to be drilling equipment. Violations are being issued for failure to tag and post the well, in accordance with OGA3211(G) and OGA3211(H). The Department recommends replacing the current well tag and adding the well posting requirements to the site.The Department requests information on each of the three tanks and the trailer on site, including identification, purpose, and if they are necessary for the production of the well. The Department recommends removing all equipment not necessary for production of the well from the site.The Department recommends the Operator maintain freeboard operations in the open top tanks in accordance with regulations under Chapter 78.56.
